newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon STARS team selected by FAA.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon STARS team selected by FAA.

text.p: Raytheon Electronic Systems said it has been awarded a contract from the Federal Aviation Administration for STARS -- the Standard Terminal Automation Replacement System -- which ultimately could be worth nearly $1 billion.
The Raytheon Co subsidiary is the prime contractor for the STARS team, which includes Hughes Electronics Corp, Sun Microsystems Inc, United Faculty Associates and Jerry Thompson Associates.
The STARS system will modernize and upgrade 331 Terminal Automation Systems for the FAA and Department of Defense.
This modernization program will replace aging terminal automation equipment with an open system architecture.

The STARS system will accept data from radars and enroute centers to provide the radar data processing display and modification of flight data, which allows control and separation of aircraft in the terminal airspace and will also assure a safe, long-term obsolescence-free operation.
STARS will provide a safe, automated system for airport approach and departure control and better on-time schedules in all weather conditions.

Boston's Logan Airport and Eglin Air Force Base in Florida will be the recipients of the first two systems in the United States. These systems will be operational in December 1998 and the total STARS program implementation will take place over a 10 year period, Raytheon said.
